title: Security contract clause matrix and prioritization journey for enterprise requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a clause-level security request matrix and end-to-end prioritization journey that maps incoming enterprise contract asks (SOC2/ISO attestation requirements, HIPAA safeguards, GDPR/DPA clauses, vendor questionnaire items) to deterministic product/ops actions and SLA templates. Goal is to reduce manual review time, increase throughput for standard asks, and ensure high-severity contractual requirements get guaranteed engineering/ops SLAs and runbook coverage.

Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of security and compliance asks via questionnaires and RFI forms. Currently intake requires significant manual triage by Security + PMs which slows contract cycles and causes inconsistent responses/SLAs. We need a reusable artifact that: (1) classifies asks into normalized clause types, (2) assigns priority and owner, (3) maps to an executable product or operational action (e.g., config change, documentation update, SLA commit, or Private deployment engagement), and (4) produces an appropriate customer-facing SLA template and timeline estimate.

Objectives:
- Define a canonical set of clause categories (e.g., Data Residency, Data Retention, Encryption in Transit, Encryption at Rest/KMS, Access Controls/SSO, Audit Logs, Incident Notification, Subprocessor Disclosure, Data Processing Addendum language).
- Create a scoring algorithm to convert questionnaire items into priority bands (P0/P1/P2) and SLAs (72h triage, 14d standard response, 60d remediation window, etc.).
- Produce three templated SLA/response bundles (Standard, Expedited, Non-negotiable/high-severity) that legal and sales can use immediately.
- Automate routing in intake system: map high-severity clauses to Security+Legal + Eng oncall, standard asks to PM/Docs + Solutions, and low-risk asks to Knowledge Base updates.
- Define measurable KPIs: time-to-first-response, time-to-resolution, percent automated-routing, and reduction in manual review hours.

Scope: Includes questionnaire CSV import parsing rules, clause taxonomy, scoring model, SLA templates, routing rules, product/ops checklist per clause, and a pilot with 3 commercial customers. Excludes changes to customer contracts/legal terms themselves (Legal to own sign-off), but includes recommended language snippets for Sales.

Deliverables:
- Clause matrix (spreadsheet) with mapping: clause-id | category | severity score | suggested product action | default SLA template id. (Drive doc link in links field.)
- Prioritization scoring doc with weights and examples.
- Three SLA/response templates (Standard/Expedited/Non-negotiable) for Sales & CS.
- Intake automation spec for engineering (routing rules + webhook payload examples).
- Runbooks for Eng/Infra for top 8 clause types (e.g., on-prem/on-VPC requirements, audit log exports, KMS integration checklist).
- Pilot report with 3 customers including time metrics and feedback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clause matrix completed and reviewed by Security and Legal.
- Scoring algorithm tested against a dataset of 120 past questionnaire items with >=85% alignment to manual historical prioritization.
- Intake automation spec merged into the intake repo and an initial routing prototype deployed to staging.
- SLA templates reviewed and approved by Legal and Sales engineering.
- Pilot demonstrates >=40% reduction in manual triage hours and meets time-to-first-response SLA for expedited band in at least 2/3 pilot customers.

Trade-offs/Notes:
- Conservative scoring reduces false negatives (escalation missed) at cost of more manual reviews; we tune thresholds post-pilot.
- Some asks (custom DPA clauses) will remain legal-only and likely require contract-level negotiation; these are flagged but not auto-approved.
- Implementing automated routing requires a small addition to intake API (webhook + clause ids) and a light-weight Rules Engine; scope avoids building an ML classifier in Phase 1 to accelerate delivery.

Dependencies:
- Legal sign-off on canonical clause taxonomy and templates.
- Security engineering time for runbook authoring and staging routing hooks.
- Intake UI/engineering for CSV upload and webhook support.

Risks:
- Misclassification could expose us to contractual commitments without legal approval; we mitigate with guardrails (human-in-loop for high-severity).
- Resource contention with concurrent SOC2 roadmap items; Security engineering to allocate dedicated 0.2 FTE during pilot.

Timeline / Milestones:
- Week 1-2: build taxonomy + initial clause matrix draft.
- Week 3: scoring algorithm + examples; SLA templates initial draft.
- Week 4: intake automation spec + routing prototype.
- Week 5-6: runbook drafting and pilot onboarding.
- Week 7: pilot measurement, adjust thresholds, Legal final sign-off.

Stakeholders: Sales (enterprise AE), Legal, Security, Security Engineering, Solutions, Documentation, Customer Success.

Primary success metric: mean manual triage hours per request reduced by >=40% after pilot and 60% of incoming requests auto-classified into actionable buckets.
